The complete selected original text is identical within the same SEC Item after removing line-leading bullet formatting and normalizing whitespace. Neither LLM agent was used for this link.

Both disclosures describe the remarketing of specific unsecured general obligation bonds issued by the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (and/or State of Oregon). The 2023 disclosure notes the remarketing of $423 million in bonds maturing in 2035/2040 with specific coupons. The 2024 disclosure notes the remarketing of $438 million of Arizona bonds maturing in 2049 with a 4.0% coupon. Both refer to the same specific facility/authority bonds being remarketed in the respective years, maintaining the same specific subject matter (Arizona/Oregon bonds remarketing).

comparisons.peer_topic: Issuance and Terms of Senior Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: On June 9, 2022, the Company issued $1.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of 3.924% Senior Notes Due 2032 and 4.393% Senior Notes Due 2052, which are general unsecured senior obligations governed by a June 9, 2022 indenture. comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the terms of unsecured debt obligations. Intel's disclosure details $423 million of unsecured general obligation bonds issued by state authorities with specific maturities (2035, 2040) and coupons (3.8%, 4.1%). Similarly, AMD discloses $1.0 billion of general unsecured senior notes (3.924% due 2032 and 4.393% due 2052). While Intel's bonds are tied to specific industrial authorities and have optional tender features, both companies utilize unsecured debt instruments with fixed coupons and semi-annual interest payments to manage capital resources.

sentences.text: In 2023, we remarketed $423 million aggregate principal amount of bonds issued by the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (the Arizona bonds) and the State of Oregon Business Development Commission (the Oregon bonds).

The bonds are unsecured general obligations in accordance with loan agreements we entered into with each of the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (CIDA) and the State of Oregon Business Development Commission.
The bonds mature in 2035 and 2040 and have 3.8% and 4.1% coupons.
On June 9, 2022, the Company issued $1.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes.
The 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes are general unsecured senior obligations of the Company.
The 3.924% and 4.393% Notes are governed by the terms of an indenture dated June 9, 2022 between the Company and US Bank Trust Company, National Association as trustee.

comparisons.peer_topic: Issuance of Senior Unsecured Notes in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: The company issued senior unsecured notes totaling $10 billion in 2024, with $5 billion issued in July and another $5 billion in October.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both issued unsecured debt in recent years to support their capital structures. Intel's disclosure refers to $423 million of unsecured general obligation bonds remarketed in 2023. Broadcom's disclosure highlights a larger scale of activity, issuing $10 billion in senior unsecured notes in 2024 ($5 billion in July and $5 billion in October). Both entities rely on unsecured credit facilities, though Broadcom's 2024 issuance was significantly larger in aggregate principal amount and involved a new issuance rather than a remarketing of previously issued bonds.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company issued $6.70 billion of senior unsecured notes and term loans, receiving $6.69 billion in cash, and prepaid $600 million of the 2024 Term Loan A principal.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both disclose significant activity in unsecured debt markets. Intel's disclosure details $423 million of unsecured general obligation bonds. Micron's disclosure reports a much larger issuance of $6.70 billion in senior unsecured notes and term loans in 2023, receiving $6.69 billion in cash. A key difference is that Micron's disclosure explicitly mentions prepaying $600 million of Term Loan A principal during this period, whereas Intel's disclosure focuses on the terms and optional tender features of the remarketed bonds without mentioning concurrent prepayments in this specific note.
